The observations point to the presence of two distinct but very similar compounds that are isomers with the same mass and nearly identical structures. In peptide synthesis, epimerization at the α-carbon during coupling is a common side reaction, producing a mixture of diastereomers. Diastereomers have different physical properties, so they can separate on a standard achiral LC column (giving two peaks), yet they share the same mass spectrum. Their NMR spectra are slightly different, leading to duplicate peaks for protons near the stereocenter, such as the α-proton. Enantiomers would not separate on an achiral column and would give identical NMR spectra in an achiral environment. A precursor would have a different mass, and "double coupling" is not a standard explanation that fits the equal mass and integral data.

Answer: D
